normalized.title: EUROPEAN ULTRA-DEEP SUB-MICRON BEAMFORMING CHIP IP CORE FOR SATCOM CONSTELLATIONS (ARTES AT 5C.539)
normalized.description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to develop a European beamforming chip IP core based on ultra-deep sub-micron technology for satcom constellations. Power consumption shall be minimised. Selectable waveform specific features shall be implemented to support a wide range of use cases including pre-coding and beam hopping. A test chip with compatible interfaces to high speed SerDes (Serialiser/Deserialiser) providing reliable connectivity for high throughput satellites of LEO and MEO constellations shall be designed and manufactured.Targeted Improvements: - Enabling a European or Canadian source of digital beamforming IP core for active phased array antennas.- Enabling features such as signal structure, beam hopping and precoding.- Minimised power consumption of less than 300mW per channel.Description: Due to the demand for large capacity and high spectral efficiencies, active array antennas are being increasingly employed for telecom satellites. These antennas are already playing an important role in next-generation high throughput satellite (HTS) communications together with the large low Earth orbit (LEO) and medium Earth orbit (MEO) constellations being implemented worldwide. Digital Beamforming (DBF) is considered the most flexible beamforming architecture and has advantages over analogue beamforming for receiving and transmitting wideband signals, and for multi-beam reconfigurable applications. However, it requires data converters and RF front-ends for each antenna element, increasing the complexity and power consumption.In this activity, a digital beamforming IP core will be developed, fabricated as a scaled Engineering Model test chip and tested based on ultra sub-micron technology (targeting 7nm or lower). Power consumption shall be minimised, targeting 300mW per channel. Selectable waveform specific features shall be implemented to support a wide range of use casesincluding pre-coding and beam hopping. The IP core shall enable Beamforming Networks with a total bandwidth scalable from GHz to hundreds of GHz for dynamic beam configuration, to achieve a BFIC of 32 GHz capacity with scalable frequency from L-Band to Ka-Band and frequency agnostic topology.This activity will be implemented in a phased approach where:- Phase 1 includes a comparative architectural study of at least four digital beam forming IC integration models. An evaluation of technology node implications shall be performed (e.g. leading-edge vs. trailing-edge). Phase 1 shall explore if a common architecture could support different use-cases (broadband, D2D) e.g. lowering DAC/ADC sampling rates and smart switching (bypassing digital mixing, decimation/interpolation) to maintain beam count while adjusting per-beam bandwidth. A system topology shall be evaluated and defined from the digital processor to the antenna for the placement of the beamforming network (daisy chain, star etc.). The output of Phase 1 is an evaluation of the critical IP blocks via design simulation concluding with tape-out of the design. Phase 1 budget is up to 1,200kEur.- In Phase 2 the architecture and technology for the beamforming chip IP shall be fully designed, implemented and tested to scaled engineering model level. This test chip will be representative of a scaled version of the final potential product. Scaled EM testing will include radiation exposure, thermal cycling, and performance benchmarking against existing space-grade beamforming chips.IP cores developed in this activity shall be available for further development by ESA Member State and Canadian industries at fair and reasonable market conditions.

This will be characterised by enhanced spatial sampling and spectral sampling compared to Sentinel-2 first generation. S2 NG will provide observations for the next generation of operational products such as landcover maps, land-change detection maps, and geophysical properties,  together with, as secondary objective, for the next generation of operational products over a larger portion of coastal and marine waters compared to Sentinel-2. S2NG will provide quantitative evidence in support to European and global policies, including the Green Deal, the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP), the EU Forest Strategy, the EU Biodiversity Strategy, the EU Soil Strategy, the EU Water Framework and the UN SDGs. The S2NG space segment is expected to comprise of a constellation of two identical satellites (A- and B-units) flying at an altitude of approximately 650 km, in a sun-synchronous orbit. Each satellite will embark a payload comprised of the Advanced Multi-Spectral Imager (AMSI) instrument with two detection chains, one for Visible and Near-Infrared (VNIR) detection and one for the Short Wavelength Infrared (SWIR) detection, with a total of 21 bands (16 in VNIR, 5 in SWIR).The ITT for the Sentinel-2 NG Phases B2/C/D/E1 is in open competition. The ITTwill cover all spacecraft development phases (B2/C/D/E1) of the complete Sentinel-2 NG Model A Spacecraft (i.e. including Payload and Spacecraft subsystems), and the Model B Spacecraft the latter through a contractual mandatory option. This ITT will be arranged in two Contractual Phases as follows: Phase 1 will include:  - all Payload Instruments activities up to the Sentinel-2 NG Model A Instrument Preliminary Design Review, and subsequent payload advanced phase C activities up to the end of the satellite Phase B2 (PDR);- all Sentinel-2 NG spacecraft activities, including the System Requirements Review (SRR), up to and including the Satellite Preliminary Design Review (PDR); and - the procurement of relevant long lead Items (LLI) for both Sentinel-2 NG Model A and Model B Spacecraft. Phase 2 will include: - All remaining Spacecraft activities up to and including the Sentinel-2 NG Model A Spacecraft Qualification and Flight Acceptance Review (QAR).Additional information: The Invitation to Tender (ITT) will be published on ESA Star. In order to access the ITT Package, Tenderers must be registered in esa-star as potential ESA suppliers. Any Tenderer, which is not yet registered with ESA as a potential supplier, must complete the online questionnaire in esa-star, https://esastar-emr.sso. esa.int/. normalized.description: Objective: To develop a representative demonstrator of a Scatterometer instrument based on a phased array with a reduced number of control points, by exploiting grating lobes.Description: For Earth Observation applications there are instruments, like Scatterometers, requiring a limited number of beams M pointing in fixed directions. A promising antenna architecture is based on an array antenna organized in interleaved subarrays (number of subarrays equal to the number of target beams M). Each subarray is having the periodic cell split in M sub-apertures. One of the M sub-apertures is occupied by a radiating element, the other M-1 slots are kept emptyto be used by the other M-1 interleaved subarrays. The dimension of the periodic cell is larger than one wavelength in order to create grating lobes exactly in the directions where the desired beams of the Scatterometer instrument are targeted. The array factor associated to the M phase centres of the M subarrays, when fed with identical phase value, creates a beam pointing at the boresight direction with radiative nulls positions coinciding with the grating lobes positions. Accordingly, when feeding the M inputs with thesame phase value a main beam in the boresight direction can be generated and the M-1 grating lobes can be cancelled by the radiative nulls. When feeding the M inputs with a linear phase in order to point the main beam exactly at one of the M possible targeted angles, the radiative nulls permit to cancel all the subarray pattern beams except the desired one. The M beams can be generated one atthe time, or simultaneously by adding a small beamforming MxM network. Possible values for M could be 3 or 5. To be noted also thatthecorresponding beams can be placed in the same azimuthal plane or not. This beamforming solution permits to reduce by a factor Mthe number of controls (phase shifters, direction couplers, amplifiers). As a consequence, a significant reduction in the cost and complexity of the entire instrument can be achieved. Reducing by a factor 3-5 the number of passive and active components in a Scatterometer instrument based on a phased array. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Instrument identification and requirements refinement. - Technology trade-off and down-selection. - Identification/optimization of most promising architectures. - Preliminary design of a baseline architecture and back-up architecture - Detailed design of a baseline architecture - Define preliminary manufacturing technique and prototype. - Definition of test and verification plan - Breadboard manufacturing and test - Results analysis and evaluation.

normalized.title: NAVISP EL1-134 ALL-WEATHER LASER TIMING AND RANGING LINKS FOR OPTICAL PNT SYSTEMS - EXPRO+
normalized.description: EL1-134 - This activity will investigate innovative techniques to enable continuous optical timing and ranging links under all weather conditions, addressing a key challenge for operational optical PNT (Positioning, Navigation, and Timing) systems. Optical satellite-to-ground links, such as those planned for ESA's OpSTAR mission, are vulnerable to atmospheric effects, particularly cloud cover, which can degrade or completely interrupt communications with an Optical Ground Station (OGS). The study will assess and experimentally demonstrate atmospheric transmission enhancement techniques designed to improve link availability under adverse weather conditions. It will evaluate whether these approaches can maintain accurate and reliable timing and ranging measurements between laser terminals representative of future operational optical PNT systems.

originalText: {"job":"institution-ESA-issued-competition","collectionState":"reconciled","verifiedOpen":false,"spaceRelevance":"not_assessed","recordType":"discovery_candidate","evidence":{"file":"institution-ESA-issued-competition/page-2-c82cdb09f779020c1ae921f4e5d913adc8a31016bec44a694c073ece3ea91192.json","sha256":"c82cdb09f779020c1ae921f4e5d913adc8a31016bec44a694c073ece3ea91192","row":30,"retrievedAt":"2026-11-25T09:30:22.175Z"},"original":{"activityNumber":"1000045730","closingDate":"2026-12-02T13:00:00","clarificationRequestDeadline":"2026-11-25T13:00:00","description":"Objective: To model the hypersonic flow around critical points of the re-entry of a upper stage vehicle, accounting for the catalytic properties of a Si-O-C ceramics, and for the chemical modifications of the surface exposed to the air.Description: There is a renewed interest in the implementation of reusable vehicles for in-orbit operation. A critical aspect in the lifetime of a space vehicle is to improve the durability of the thermal protection structures, to limit the replacement of the thermal shield. Ultra-high temperature ceramics (UHTC) materials, based on the Si-O-C compounds with dedicated coatings (boride, molybdenum etc.) demonstrated to be a good choice, due to their capability to resist and survive above 1500 K. To fully evaluate the response of any material in suchextreme operating conditions, it is also imperative to determine the catalysis in high temperature gas, strongly affecting the surface heat flux. Moreover, the interaction of the material coatings with dissociated gases such as oxygen and nitrogen, induces variations on the material properties. normalized.description: The frontiers for the deployment of 5G cellular networks have grown beyond the limits of the Earth's atmosphere. The 3GPP cellular technologies have become attractive for exploration missions, such as Moon or Mars, as they can provide a standardised scalable, secure, high-capacity, and reliable connectivity. For Moon, the Space Frequency Coordination Group (SFCG) has recently identified several bands for Lunar missions for the deployment of existing Earth communication protocols that includes the cellular element. In parallel to the connectivity, 5G networks can also be used to enhance the performance of navigation services fores een in LunaNet.The communication services will be primarily delivered by satellite-based solutions (already identified in the LunaNet architecture for the Moon). However, although the lunar relay satellites could technically provide surface-to-surface communications for a small number of users, such approach does not scale well as the number of users increases.To serve larger number of users, wireless cellularnetworks on the lunar surface are foreseen. With such deployments, an opportunity to offer 5G space user terminals emerges on the market. A new space-grade 5G user terminal will thus need to be developed, leveraging the technologies from 5G ground terminals, and making them available for exploration missions. This activity will design, manufacture, and test an engineering model of a 5G user terminal in FR1 for exploration missions. To achieve this, the activity willleverage on the current standards, techniques, and technologies. The activity will:- Review and consolidate the connectivity use cases of 3GPP networks in exploration missions (Moon and/or Mars)- Identify potential future exploration missions- Define and study architecture and scenarios of 5G cellular networks that could provide connectivity and enhanced navigation.- Design and implement an engineering model of 5G user equipment, including a test equipment, for connectivity in exploration missions.- Test the connectivity and positioning performance of the 3GPP networks using the developed test equipment.- Develop a roadmap to reach a flight model with integration of LunaNet navigation receiver capabilities
